pue.boundary: CoreWeave active Q2 2026 fleet: total data-center energy divided by IT-equipment energy over identical sites and periods
pue.basis: The 10-K says CoreWeave works with partners to track PUE and is collecting necessary data, but gives no operational value. No current site facility MWh, IT MWh or IT-energy weights support a fleet value or range. Training efficiency, active power, design targets and generation ratios are not PUE.
pue.aggregation: sum(matched total data-center MWh)/sum(matched IT-equipment MWh)

model.revenue_scope: External recognized AI compute after non-compute removal. Total cloud revenue is only a ceiling; the recent signed-contract rate is a separate forward commercial measure.
model.capacity_time_basis: 91 days. More than 1.0GW at March 31, 1.5GW at June 30, nearly 500MW added in Q2 and more than 300MW activated in June. Exact activation days and IT/facility boundary are unavailable, so no point average is selected; 1.0-1.5GW is only a broad timing bound.

assumptions.basis: Quarter-times-four convention; not guidance, backlog conversion or exit ARR.
Broad opening/exit bound only. More than 300MW activated in June makes an unqualified midpoint misleading.

sensitivities.reason: No supported PUE, physical utilization or active-power boundary; arbitrary axes imply false precision.

missing: comparable realized compute or token price decline
jevons.exclusion: July's approximately 25% SKU price increase is not a token-price decline.

structured_deals.economic_effect: Recent Q3 3-6 month contracts were signed near $40M annualized per MW of power required for related clusters. This current tightness signal carries repricing/rollover risk and is not recognized revenue per effective IT MW.
Committed contracts generated 98% of Q2 revenue; about 70% of Q2 signed deals included customer prepayment. Prepayments help funding timing but are not recognized revenue.
A100 renewal runs through 2029 at a three-year term priced in line with typical one-year pricing; a three-year H200 renewal carried a premium to the original contract. MW and margin are undisclosed.

One 393MW undelivered site has rent capped at $14.7B over 16 years and is excluded from the $35.5B uncommenced estimate. Other uncertain leases cover 355MW, plus $0.5B-$1.2B of separate equipment commitments.

$4.2B principal produced $4.137B net before other expenses; $566.2M funded capped calls, leaving derived $3.5708B before remaining expenses. Derived annual cash coupon is $120.75M. Use is general-purpose.
$2.6B can fund customer-contract GPUs/infrastructure at SOFR+5.50%, with guarantees, pledged assets and 1.35x minimum DSCR.
About $21B of dedicated capacity through December 2032. Matched MW, PUE and price schedule remain undisclosed.

findings: Recent 3-6 month Q3 contracts priced near $40M of annualized revenue per MW of power required for related clusters. This is a current contracted-rate signal, not recognized revenue per IT/effective MW.
Fleet PUE remains not disclosed; no defensible low/base/high range exists. The old arbitrary PUE/utilization sensitivity is superseded without a numerical replacement.

Q2 total cloud revenue annualizes to $10.3B; against only a broad 1.0-1.5GW timing bound, it gives a noncanonical $6.87M-$10.30M per reported-active-power MW-year ceiling. More than 300MW activated in June prevents selecting the old 1.25GW midpoint.
Canonical compute revenue per effective utilized IT MW remains blank because compute-only revenue, power boundary, dated IT-MW cohorts, matched PUE and physical utilization are missing.
$4.2B of 2.875% converts improved liquidity, but $566.2M funded capped calls and one undelivered 393MW site alone has rent capped at $14.7B/16 years.
gaps: Compute-only Q2 recognized revenue after storage, networking and software.
Active-power metering boundary, dated activations and period-average active AI IT MW.
Matched total/IT MWh, operational PUE, IT-energy weights and physical utilization.
Underlying cohort MW, architecture, customers, margin, prepayment, acceptance, termination, renewal and resale terms for the $40M/MW-year rate.
Site PPAs, utility delivery, SPV/VIE debt, guarantees and lessor construction-cost waterfalls for the 393MW and 355MW cohorts.
GPU economic/replacement life by generation; six years is only an accounting life.
Comparable token/task price-volume data and open/proprietary mix for an exact Jevons test.
